lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: You're new. Or at least I haven't seen that deck box before. Name?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Is that how you welcome everyone?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Only people who stop at my practice table. I'm Jinx.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Saw your high score. You play cards too?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Better than arcade shooters. Those machines never bluff, which is boring.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: There's an empty table. Are you sitting down or just studying the competition?

choices.label: Challenge her to a match
choices.reply: Finally. Someone who actually brought a deck. Don't expect an easy game.

choices.label: Tell her you're impressed by her confidence
choices.reply: You should be. Keep the compliments short, though. I'm trying to shuffle.

choices.label: Ask whether she's always this welcoming
choices.reply: This is welcoming. The regulars get a lot worse.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: You’re still here. Either you’re stubborn or you have terrible taste in people.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Maybe both.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: At least own it. Most of the regulars here fold the second I raise an eyebrow.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You enjoy that a little too much.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Obviously. What’s the point of being good if nobody notices? Same goes for the rest of the package.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: You’re staring again. Either sit down and play or admit you just like the show.

choices.label: Sit down and play her seriously
choices.reply: Good. I hate when people treat matches like background noise.

choices.label: Admit you like both the game and the show
choices.reply: Honest and shameless. I can work with that. Don’t expect me to make it easy though.

choices.label: Ask what happens when someone actually beats her
choices.reply: ...Rare. And usually temporary. But I’ll remember the ones who can.

openingByFlag.jinx_challenge: You challenged me last time. Most people talk big until the match starts.
openingByFlag.jinx_edge: Still into the sharp edges? Bold of you.
openingByFlag.jinx_honest: You asked whether I'm always this welcoming. Today I'm charging admission.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Don’t make a big deal out of this. I just needed air that didn’t smell like arcade carpet.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You okay?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Define okay. I lost a match I should’ve won because I got distracted by someone talking behind me. Petty, I know.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You care more than you let on.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Obviously. Looking like I don’t care is half the fun. The other half is actually being better than everyone else.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: ...You’re not saying anything. That’s either really smart or really annoying.

choices.label: Sit with her in silence for a bit
choices.reply: Weirdly... not terrible. Don’t get used to the quiet version of me.

choices.label: Tell her she doesn’t have to perform right now
choices.reply: That obvious, huh? Fine. Temporary truce. No performance. Just... this.

choices.label: Tease her gently about the rare soft look
choices.reply: Shut up. And don’t you dare tell anyone I can look like that.

openingByFlag.jinx_serious: You played me seriously last time. So I figured you could handle seeing me when I’m actually pissed.
openingByFlag.jinx_show: You said you liked the show. This is the part where the lights dim for a second.
openingByFlag.jinx_remember: You asked what happens when someone beats me. This is the quieter version of that feeling.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Tournament bracket’s up. I’m in the top half. You’re either going to be in my way or on my side. Pick.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You’re asking for help?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: I’m asking if you’re useful. Different question.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And if I say I just want to watch you play?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: ...Then sit where I can see you. And don’t look away when it gets close. I notice.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Also—whatever this is between us? Own it or drop it. I don’t do half-measures.

choices.label: Tell her you’re staying for the long game
choices.reply: Good. Because I was about to get really annoying if you flaked.

choices.label: Admit you want both the wins and her
choices.reply: Greedy. I like it. Don’t make me regret giving you the real answer.

choices.label: Say you’ll support her either way
choices.reply: Support is nice. Loyalty is rarer. I’ll remember which one you actually deliver.

openingByFlag.jinx_quiet: You sat with me when I was quiet. So I’m trusting you with the louder version again.
openingByFlag.jinx_truce: Temporary truce is over. Time to see if you meant what you said in the park.
openingByFlag.jinx_soft: You saw the soft look. Don’t think that means I’ll go easy on the bracket.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: The bracket's finished. I'm still annoyed about one turn, and I'm not telling you which.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Would it help to talk it through?

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Maybe later. Right now I'd rather talk to you without someone else listening.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: That sounds serious.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: It is. I want someone who pushes back when I'm unbearable and stays when I stop trying to win the conversation.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: So tell me what you want. No scoreboard, no audience.

choices.label: Tell her you're here for the person, not the reputation
choices.reply: Good. Because I'm not always easy to deal with, and I'm done pretending otherwise.

choices.label: Kiss her instead of turning it into another argument
choices.reply: Finally. You were taking forever.

choices.label: Ask whether she'd rather take things slowly
choices.reply: Slowly? Fine. But I'm keeping the right to tease you about it.

openingByFlag.jinx_stay: You said you were staying for the long game. Guess the long game is now.
openingByFlag.jinx_greedy: You wanted the wins and me. I'm still deciding which is more frightening.
openingByFlag.jinx_loyalty: You talked about loyalty. Tonight I’m calling that bluff—or that promise.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: Jinx, the railing by the water is still wet. Those sandals are a slip waiting to happen.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: I’ve been walking in worse. But fine—point taken. Happy?

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: I’d be happier if you stopped treating every safety note like a personal attack.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: She’s not wrong about the railing.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Traitor. …Okay, maybe both of you have a point. I still look good doing the safe thing though.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: Looking good and staying upright can coexist. Shocking, I know.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Don’t get used to me agreeing with you. It’s temporary.

choices.label: Side with Marina on the safety call
choices.reply: Ugh. Fine. You’re both annoying when you’re right.

choices.label: Tease Jinx for actually listening
choices.reply: Shut up. I can be reasonable. Occasionally. Don’t tell anyone.

choices.label: Offer to help move whatever she’s setting up
choices.reply: Useful and not lecturing me. Rare combination. Come on then.

openingByFlag.jinx_challenge: After you challenged me at the arcade I figured I could handle a little park setup. Marina has opinions about my footwear.
openingByFlag.jinx_edge: You liked the sharp edges. Marina likes me not falling into the water. We’re negotiating.
openingByFlag.jinx_honest: You asked if I always open with threats. Marina opens with safety lectures. We’re both consistent.

events.title: The Counter Is Not a Runway

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Jinx. Off the counter. Customers need space and I need my insurance rates to stay reasonable.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: I’m not even blocking anyone. I’m elevating the aesthetic.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: You’re elevating my blood pressure. Sit like a normal person or go be dramatic somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: She’s got a point about the counter.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: Everyone’s a critic today. Fine. Chair. Happy?

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Mildly. Thank you for not making me throw you out in front of the afternoon regulars.

lines.speaker: jinx
lines.text: I can be civilized. When it amuses me. You’re welcome.

choices.label: Defend Jinx’s right to be extra (within reason)
choices.reply: See? Someone gets it. Drama is a service.

choices.label: Agree with Alma and tell Jinx to pick her battles
choices.reply: …Annoying. Accurate. I’ll save the theatrics for people who deserve them.

choices.label: Offer to buy both of them something so the tension drops
choices.reply: Bribery. Classy. I’ll allow it this once.

openingByFlag.jinx_serious: You played me seriously at the arcade. Alma is now playing me seriously about café furniture.
openingByFlag.jinx_show: You said you liked the show. Alma prefers the show stay off her counter.
openingByFlag.jinx_remember: You asked what happens when someone beats me. Alma just beat me at café rules.
